review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked each @[simp] lemma against core Lean and Mathlib uses. I could not run Lean, so nothing below was tested.

- `exists_const_iff` is `@[simp low]` with an explicit comment, so `exists_prop` and core's `exists_const` fire first. It is switched off with `-exists_const_iff` in two places, one in Algebra/Category/Ring/FinitePresentation.lean and one in Algebra/Order/BigOperators/Group/Finset.lean. That fits a deliberate low-priority default.
- `Nonempty.exists` and `Nonempty.exists` against `exists_prop` for a constant body: both routes seem to reach `Nonempty α ∧ q`, either directly or through `exists_const_iff`, so I see no cycle and no conflict.
- `nonempty_subtype` against `Set.nonempty_coe_sort` and `Finset.nonempty_coe_sort`: `Set.nonempty_coe_sort` is not `@[simp]`. The Finset version carries the comment "Not `@[simp]` since `nonempty_subtype` already is." So there is one canonical rule and no competition.
- `Classical.nonempty_pi` is not simp. Mathlib's `isEmpty_pi` and `nonempty_fun` (both simp, in Basic/IsEmpty/Basic.lean) cover the pi cases, and Order/Filter/Map.lean uses it in reverse (`simp [← Classical.nonempty_pi]`). Making it simp could clash with those, so I would not add the attribute.
- `exists_true_iff_nonempty` is not simp. A plain `∃ _ : α, True` should already reduce to `Nonempty α` through `exists_const_iff` and `and_true`. The lemma is passed explicitly to simp in Topology/Connected/PathConnected.lean and Order/Filter/IsBounded.lean, which suggests redundancy at most. I could not show that it hurts or that an attribute would help.
- `nonempty_psigma`, `nonempty_pprod`, `nonempty_psum`, `nonempty_plift`, `nonempty_sigma`, `nonempty_sum`, `nonempty_prod` and `nonempty_ulift` all rewrite toward the structurally simpler form and terminate.

I have no concrete simp-interface improvement that I can support.
